tickets.title: A grok role runs a brief end to end like pi imp
tickets.what:
the owner registers a role whose harness is an interactive CLI (`harness: "cli"`, `agent: "grok"`,
model, thinking, can_continue, idle grace, extra args) and dispatches it with `hud_create` like any pi role. The MCP
opens the job's herdr tab, starts grok with the role's model/effort and its bypass flag (nothing else), checks for
the directory-trust dialog (decline and fail with a clear reason if shown), submits the brief prompt, and hands the
job to a per-job supervisor that drives STATUS.json from herdr's status events as in the feature spec: working →
idle_grace when report.md is written → `/quit` and closed when the grace ends unused; the existing watcher reaps the
tab. The brief prompt points the worker at a harness-neutral implementer instruction file shipped with the HUD
(pi-roles' implementer rules without pi-only tools) and at the brief. `hud_roster` and the Project tab show the role's
harness, agent kind, model and thinking; `hud_create` accepts `model`/`thinking` overrides for CLI roles (pi launch
switches and `pi_args` stay pi-only). A `grok-imp` role (grok-4.7, high, can continue) ships with the HUD.

See `.scratch/cli-workers/spec.md` for the role file shape, per-kind facts, the STATUS keys and the lifecycle.

tickets.title: CLI jobs continue, stop and fail like pi jobs
tickets.what:
during idle grace, `hud_send` continues a CLI job that can continue: the agent turns working, the
job goes back to `working`, and the next done is judged against the report as it was when that turn started. While
working, `hud_send` types the message into the agent (queued, as for pi). `hud_close` on a working CLI job stops it
promptly (pi-role-reap's SIGTERM via the recorded pid and start time) and the job ends `stopped`; on an idle-grace job
it quits and closes. Closing the tab or the CLI exiting on its own ends the job `failed` ("agent exited" / "tab
closed"). If the supervisor process itself dies, the watcher notices on its next scan and marks the job failed
instead of keeping it open forever. The watcher's "move job-dir session files into pi's store before deleting" step
runs for pi jobs only.

acceptance.text: Continuation in grace, with a second report check, covered by tests with a fake herdr
hud_close: working → stopped; idle_grace → closed; tab closed → failed; CLI exit → failed
A dead supervisor is detected by the watcher and the job settles failed
Session preservation skipped for non-pi jobs; pi behaviour unchanged (existing tests)

tickets.title: CLI workers can ask the orchestrator, and a stuck CLI asks for the owner
tickets.what:
a CLI worker asks a question by running the HUD's `hud-ask` command (named by absolute path in
the brief instructions). The question lands in the job's `qa/` in pi-roles' exact format, the orchestrator pane gets
pi-roles' one-line QUESTION notice, `hud_read` lists it, `hud_respond` answers it and the waiting command prints the
answer to the worker; with no answer in 20 minutes it prints the default and the worker carries on and records the
open question in its report. When herdr reports the CLI `blocked` mid-turn (an approval or question UI the bypass flag
did not cover), the panel shows the job as needing the owner and the orchestrator pane gets one line naming the job
and pane; once the CLI works again the job is `working`.

tickets.title: A CLI turn that ends without a report is not a failed job
tickets.what:
**Why:** herdr's `done` is a screen heuristic for "the turn looks finished". A CLI agent waiting on a background
command (agy, 2026-11-14: tests in the background, "Waiting for the test run to complete") shows `done` too. The
supervisor treated `done` without a report as the end of the job, failed it and sent `/quit`, killing 18 minutes of
work in progress (ROLE-BIND 01, job j2341a54f3f7c0e5d).

**What to build:** in `packages/hud-mcp/bin/hud-cli.mjs` the report is the completion signal; herdr's status only says
whether the agent is busy.
- A turn that ends without a new report keeps the job open (`working`, card detail "turn ended, no report yet"); the
  supervisor keeps waiting. A report that appears at any time (also while herdr says working or done) settles the
  turn as today (idle grace or closed).
- Background work counts as busy (owner 2026-11-14: Claude Code and agy park background processes and wake themselves
  when they finish). At the start of each turn the supervisor records the CLI process's descendants (MCP servers and
  other long-lived helpers); while any newer descendant is alive, or herdr says working, the job is busy and the
  no-report clock does not run. A self-wake (herdr back to working) simply continues the turn.
- If the agent stays quiet (herdr not working, no new descendants) with no report for the role's idle grace
  (default 10 minutes), the job turns `waiting_orchestrator` with one notice line to the main session ("quiet without
  a report; hud_send to continue or hud_close to stop"). If the agent wakes by itself afterwards, the job is working
  again.
- The HUD only observes here (owner 2026-11-14: do not interfere with the model's run): it sends the worker nothing
  on its own (no nudge) and does not change the worker instructions for this; the main session decides what to say.
  It never quits an agent because a report is missing; only stop, close, tab closed, agent exit or the post-report
  grace end it.

**Size:** about 50 source lines; fake-herdr tests in thin-mcp

Legacy role: agy-imp (gemini-4-hydrogen-high)

Legacy Blocked by: ROLE-BIND 01 (same files: hud-cli.mjs, thin-mcp.test.mjs)

tickets.title: A quiet CLI job without a report gets one Decision API choice
tickets.what:
**Why:** owner 2026-11-14 (spec §2, "One exception"): the main session should not have to handle every CLI worker that
stops without a report. Cost is not a concern; predictability is.

**What to build:** at the point where ticket 09 turns a job `waiting_orchestrator` ("quiet without a report"), the
supervisor first asks the Decision API (the provider chosen in Settings, through `src/jev/`) one choice question with
probabilities. Input: the last 60 lines of the pane (`herdr pane read --source recent`), job state, whether a
background child is alive, minutes quiet. Options and actions:
- `still-working` (waiting on background work or thinking) → keep waiting one more idle grace, then ask again (at most
  3 questions per job);
- `finished-no-report` → send the fixed prompt "Write your report to <path> now; if work remains, finish it first."
  once per job, then wait as after any turn;
- `failed` (quota/rate limit on screen) → only when the quoted screen line matches the quota regex
  (`src/roles/exhausted.ts` `isQuotaFailure`): fail the job with that line as reason and mark the place exhausted
  (ROLE-BIND); a `failed` choice whose line does not match → `needs-human` (owner 2026-11-14);
- `needs-human` (a terminal prompt, a question, or unclear) → `waiting_orchestrator` with the notice, as 09.
Below 0.8 probability for the top option, without a key, over the call cap or on any error → `needs-human`. The
choice, its probability and the action go into STATUS (`quiet_decision`) and show on the card and in the Inspector.
Decision calls count under a `quiet-job` feature in Settings' per-feature breakdown.

Also check whether `mistral/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` with reasoning off gives structured output and option
probabilities through the Mistral API; if it does, add it as a Decision API provider choice in Settings (keys from
`~/.hud/credentials.env`); if not, record why in the comments and leave the providers as they are.

**Size:** about 120 source lines; tests with a fake herdr and a fake
decision provider (no real calls)

Legacy role: agy-imp (gemini-4-hydrogen-high)

comments.text: **Mistral DeepSeek check (`deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017`, reasoning off):** Tested live against `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` using `MISTRAL_API_KEY` from `~/.hud/credentials.env`. `POST /v1/decisions` returned `404` (`no Route matched with those values`). `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: "deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017"`, `reasoning_effort: "none"`, and `response_format: { type: "json_schema", strict: true, ... }` returned `200` (`reasoning_tokens: 0`, valid JSON `{"choice": "failed"}`), but adding `logprobs: true, top_logprobs: 5` returned `400` (`code: "3051"`, `"Logprobs are not enabled for this model"`). Structured output works, option probabilities do not, so Decision API providers remain unchanged (`gemini`, `openai`, `typesafe`).
